answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with quadratic identity staking: the first identity posts a small bond, and each additional identity by the same operator must post a bond growing with the square of its index, so a tenth identity costs a hundred times the first. The velvet glove of low entry fees hides an iron ledger, since bonds lock for a full epoch. An attacker spinning up a forge of fake agents faces exploding capital costs, while honest single-identity agents pay almost nothing. Like water slowly carving karst, the cost erodes only the attacker's position.
